question: Israeli intelligence recently announced that 12 staff members of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) were allegedly involved in the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023. UN Secretary General, António Guterres, said that ‘any UN employee involved in acts of terror will be held accountable, including through criminal prosecution’.

Several countries including Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States, and EU Member States such as Austria, Finland, France, Germany, Italy and the Netherlands, have announced that they will temporarily be suspending payments to UNRWA, pending the outcome of an in-depth investigation.

Given that, as mentioned in the EU-UNRWA Joint Declaration 2021-2024, the EU is one of the agency’s top annual donors and that the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy / Vice-President of the Commission, Josep Borrell Fontelles, announced the mobilisation of an additional EUR 10 million to the agency on 31 October 2023, can he answer the following questions: 1.
Will the EU suspend funding to UNRWA until matter is clarified, as several Member States have already done?
What actions will it take to support a swift, comprehensive and independent investigation, also with a view to ensuring that no EU money lands in the hands of the terrorist organisation Hamas?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.7.2024) The EU expressed grave concern with regards to the very serious allegations made on 24 January 2024 against 12 staff of the United Nations (UN) Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA).

The EU took note of the decision by the UNRWA Commissioner-General to immediately terminate the contracts of eight staff in the interest of the Agency, and the decision to refer the matter to the UN Office of Internal Oversight Services.

The EU also welcomed the appointment by the UN Secretary General of an independent review panel led by former French Minister Catherine Colonna to assess if UNRWA is doing its outmost to ensure its neutrality and respond to allegations of breaches to the principle of neutrality.

The Commission is strongly committed to the fight against terrorism and has engaged with UNRWA Commissioner-General and welcomed his decision to tackle the serious issues at stake. Letters outlining the way forward with all the measures and procedures for the Commission’s funding for UNRWA were exchanged on 1 and 6 March 2024.

To disburse the first tranche, the Commission requested the following: agreement by UNRWA on the three workstreams (the screening of UNRWA staff; system audit; reinforcement of the department of internal investigations and ethics office) and the signature of the EU-UNRWA contribution agreement; declaration in writing by UNRWA that up-to-date, necessary and proportionate information on staff has been shared with host countries and Israel and will be done on a quarterly basis; and the adoption by UNRWA of a concept note detailing how to strengthen the department of internal oversight services, including the establishment of a new neutrality investigation unit and ethics office.
Following UNRWA’s positive engagement and fulfilment of these agreed conditions, the Commission paid a first tranche of EUR 50 million out of the EUR 82 million foreseen for UNRWA for 2024.

Disbursement of the second tranche was conditional on the following: the Agency ensures the screening and vetting system against relevant EU sanctions list in place; UNRWA provides a progress report on the state of implementation of the concept note on how to strengthen its department of internal oversight services and ethics departments; an action plan is adopted by UNRWA to implement the recommendations of the UN independent review.

Following UNRWA’s fulfilment of the above conditions, the Commission processed the first tranche of EUR 50 million on 7 March 2024, and the second tranche of EUR 16 million on 31 May 2024, respectively. Disbursement of the third tranche of EUR 16 million is subject to the implementation of the agreement with UNRWA and the Agency’s compliance with the agreed conditions and milestones.

Furthermore, the Commission has allocated over EUR 290 million in humanitarian aid for Palestinians since the beginning of the conflict. EU humanitarian aid to Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank continues unabated through EU partner organisations, and also includes a further contracting of EUR 16 million (separate from the payments described above) that

UNRWA received from the Commission’s humanitarian aid budget for food, medical and nonfood items, shelter, as well as education and psycho-social support to civilians in Gaza. The EU recognises UNRWA’s vital role in the humanitarian response in Gaza, and that it also plays a crucial role for stability in the region1. This was reiterated by the European Council on 21 March 2024, when EU leaders stressed that the services UNRWA provides in Gaza and across the region are essential2.
